tob-10455: Kabir was a fifteenth-century Indian weaver-poet whose songs mocked the rituals of both Hindus and Muslims while celebrating a direct, loving experience of God. His verses — spare, earthy, and unforgettable — speak of the divine as an intimate presence beyond all temples and mosques. Rabindranath Tagore’s English renderings helped carry Kabir’s voice to the wider world.
tob-11055: Rudolf Steiner’s handbook promises a practical path to spiritual perception — exercises in concentration, meditation, and moral development meant to awaken ‘higher’ faculties of the soul. Written for beginners in his Anthroposophical movement, it lays out the inner training behind his teachings. The book became the standard manual for students of Steiner’s esoteric philosophy.
tob-4055: Anthropogenesis, the second volume of the Secret Doctrine, tells Blavatsky’s odd history of mankind — seven root races unfolding over ages, from airy spirit-forms to modern man. Atlantis and Lemuria loom large in her tale. Fanciful or not, it moved a whole crop of writers, painters, and seekers.
tob-13155: Legge’s Analects give the Master’s sayings in the great China-scholar’s careful English — his talks with learners on worth, study, and rule. Drawn from the Chinese Classics, this choice distills the teaching that shaped the East. The Analects stay the most quoted book in Chinese story.
tob-4155: Anna Kingsford and Edward Maitland’s Perfect Way sets forth their Christ-mystery — ‘the finding of Christ’ by hidden reading of writ. Kingsford, trail-blazing woman leech and seeress, claimed heaven’s warrant for their word. The book grew a classic of Victorian wonder-godliness.
tob-4255: Newbell Puckett’s Southland Black Beliefs — 1926 — is the trail-book on black American folk-faith, spell-work, and old wives’ tales. His field-gleanings set down conjure, haunts, and church-life at large. The book founded black folk-belief study. A landmark of American folk-lore.
tob-13455: The Liezi is the Tao-way classic laid to Lie Yukou — tales and teachings of the wise man, on unforcedness, dreams, and the Way. This olden text stands beside the Tao Te Ching and Chuang Tzu. The book is a treasure of early Tao thought.
cia-0000108155: A March 1958 National Intelligence Estimate on the likely economic effects of cutting East-West trade ties. These estimates were the intelligence community's most formal product — the collective judgment of every agency. This one weighed what would happen if the Cold War's economic iron curtain slammed fully shut.
cia-0000112355: An August 1989 report on a UFO sighted over Urumqi, in China's far-western Xinjiang region, on the evening of September 6. Frontier cities saw strange skies too. The entry files Central Asia's lights alongside all the others — the archive's net was cast worldwide.
cia-0000115455: A January 1986 National Intelligence Estimate on prospects for Guatemala's new government. After decades of military rule, civilians were taking office — but the army still held the real power. The estimate weighed whether democracy could survive in a country built for dictatorship.
cia-0000117855: An August 1985 document, title deleted, containing answers to questions posed to Colonel Oliver North. North would become famous in the Iran-Contra scandal a year later. The censored title guards the subject, but the date places it in the thick of the covert operations that would explode into scandal.
cia-0000126955: A May 1961 forecast of short-term prospects in Haiti. Papa Doc Duvalier's terror state was tightening its grip, and Washington was calculating. The document peers into the near future of the hemisphere's poorest nation — and finds little hope.
cia-0000132455: A February 1960 study of communist influence in Cuba. How red was the revolution? Washington debated; Havana denied. The document weighs the evidence: the party's men, the party's methods, the party's shadow over the island.
cia-0000132655: A 1961 report on Cuban communists explaining their successes to foreign comrades. The party was taking credit for the revolution — and teaching its methods abroad. The document is the boast, translated: the victors, instructing.
cia-0000134255: Item 21 in a 1960 Latin America series: the prospective Cuban ambassador to Washington. An ambassador to a country about to break relations — the posting was doomed. The document is the appointment: the envoy, named — for a mission already failing.
cia-0000136255: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LANGEVIN with special instructions for broadcasts following D-something — the truncated title cuts off the word. The post-invasion airwaves, scripted. The entry is the instruction: the aftermath, broadcast.
cia-0000136355: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CADICK on OKYOKE's interests and SKIMMER/SYNCARP basics — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The cryptonyms' concerns. The entry is the brief: the interests, noted.
cia-0000136855: A 1954 cable on Guatemalan white paper charges. The propaganda duel, documented. The document is the charge: the paper, answered.
un-ga-res-1755: Resolution 1755 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1962. The decolonization decade's Assembly at work. The number and year are certain; the content lives in the text.
un-ga-res-a-69-55: General Assembly Resolution A/69/55, adopted in 2014. One of the 69th session's numbered acts. The entry records the designation and year — nothing more, nothing invented.
un-sc-res-255: Security Council Resolution 255, adopted in 1968. The late-sixties Council deliberated. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-455: Security Council Resolution 455, adopted in 1979 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1355: Security Council Resolution 1355, adopted in 2001 — aligned. The new century's Council at work. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1855: Security Council Resolution 1855, cataloged with the year 2009 — the numbering suggests 2008, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
cia-0000132755: A 1961 CIA file titled Cuba, numbered 0000132755. The spare title, the number — the file behind them. The entry is the marker: the subject, Cuba.
cia-0000135755: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135755. The invasion year's papers continued. The document is the continuation: the papers, kept.
cia-0000136755: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136755, the archive's date uncertain. The roughly dated set. The entry is the roughness: the date, soft.
plos-pone-0000055: A 2006 PLOS ONE study on monitoring the T-cell receptor repertoire at single-clone resolution. Watching the immune system's diversity one clone at a time. The paper is the monitoring: the repertoire, resolved.
cia-0000137455: An estimated 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000137455, date approximate. The circa training papers. The document is the circa: the dating, soft.

frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d155: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 21, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 155. A third that day. The message is the tripling: the correspondence, intense.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d255: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 23, 1943 — Document 255. The Allied planners, minuted. The minutes are the combined: the chiefs, Allied.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d355: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 355. The connective tissue. The note is the tissue: the documents, joined.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d455: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 455. The editors' span. The note is the span: the gap, crossed.
arxiv-2605-09055: AI agents that need to touch real hardware — GPUs, sensors — face a discovery problem: what is plugged in and how is it controlled? Quilee Simeon, Justin M. Wei, and Yile Fan propose the Octopus Protocol: one-shot hardware discovery and control via infrastructure-as-prompts. The 2026 paper gives agents a standard handshake for the physical world.
arxiv-2605-09155: Every algebraic curve has a Jacobian — a geometric object encoding its secrets — and generalized versions stretch the concept further. Benjamin Castle, Ishai Dan-Cohen, and Assaf Hasson study a curve and its abstract generalized Jacobian. The 2026 paper is algebraic geometry on curves and their shadows.
arxiv-2605-09755: The power method finds dominant eigenvectors slowly; randomized sketching can speed it up dramatically. Shabarish Chenakkod and Michał Dereziński accelerate the power method with fast sketching for stronger low-rank approximation. The 2026 paper is fast, practical randomized numerical linear algebra.
arxiv-2605-09955: Subjective NLP tasks split annotators along real perspectival lines; majority voting erases the meaningful disagreement. Tadesse Destaw Belay, Ibrahim Said Ahmad, Idris Abdulmumin, and colleagues cluster by agreement instead. The 2026 paper models annotator perspectives beyond the majority. It honors disagreement instead of averaging it away.
plos-pone-0003455: Infection researchers explained why flesh-eating strep beats the immune system in this 2008 paper. Invasive group A streptococcus disarms neutrophils, the white blood cells first on the scene, by switching on multiple virulence factors at once. The finding shows how the bacterium overwhelms frontline defenders, turning routine sore-throat germs into killers in severe invasive disease.
plos-pone-0003555: Bioinformaticians proved different machines can agree in this 2008 methods paper. Gene-expression data from two rival microarray platforms lined up when analyzed through their parametric framework, yielding coincident results. The work reassures researchers that biological truth survives the switch between technologies, as long as the statistics are sound.
plos-pone-0003655: In 2008, Griguer, Oliva, and Gobin reframed a brain-tumor marker. CD133 was thought to flag cancer stem cells in glioma, but the team showed it instead marks cells under energy stress, starved of power in low-oxygen pockets. The finding retools a famous label: CD133 signals a tumor's energy crisis, not its root.
plos-pone-0003755: In 2008, Ospina, Seida, and Clark sifted the evidence on autism therapies. Their systematic review asked which behavioral and developmental interventions truly ease core autism symptoms. The careful sorting separates supported approaches from hype in a field full of claims.
plos-pone-0003855: A 2008 cell biology paper gave a centriole protein its job description. Mikael Le Clech showed CAP350 keeps centriolar tubules stable and helps assemble centrioles, the cell's organizing centers. The finding fills in how these nine-triplet cylinders get built right.
plos-pone-0003955: In 2008, Epstein, Parker, and Cummings modeled fear spreading alongside disease. Their math coupled contagion dynamics of panic with those of pathogens. The dual-spread model shows epidemics of fear can outrun the germs themselves.
plos-pone-0004055: In 2008, Capra, Skrovanek, and Kruglyak compared two worm strains growing up. They profiled gene expression across development in two C. elegans isolates. Timing differences in gene activity clearly separated the two worm strains. The careful comparison shows development itself evolving between close relatives.
plos-pone-0004155: In 2009, Levin, Hayouka, and Helfer turned HIV's own tools against it. Peptides from HIV-1 integrase bound Rev and boosted viral genome integration sharply. The integrase-derived fragments hijacked a key viral partner protein. The odd paradox points to new antiviral angles.
plos-pone-0004255: In 2009, a team found ghost skins after cell division. Nuclear envelope scraps proved fluid and rich in sterols. The leftover sheets carried rare lipid signals too. The find reframes what survives mitosis. The skins may seed the next nuclear envelope.
plos-pone-0004355: In 2009, Battaglia, Benzoubir, and Nobilet found a virus flipping a signal. Liver cancer-derived hepatitis C core proteins shifted TGF-beta responses toward tumor growth. The suppressor signal became a promoter. The flip explains HCV-driven cancer. The work pinpoints how chronic infection turns malignant.
plos-pone-0337255: Interventional oncology — treating cancer through tiny incisions with image guidance — needs a research agenda. This paper published the protocol for DEFINE-IO, a national consensus exercise to set essential priorities for future investigation. Locking the method in advance keeps the consensus honest.
plos-pone-0348455: Controlling how fast proteins get made could unlock biology in neglected species. This paper built a trainable language model that generates upstream untranslated region sequences to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms. The tool gives researchers a dial for protein production precisely where no dial existed before.
plos-pone-0358555: Eliminating measles and rubella is a long, grinding campaign. This paper tracked Lesotho’s progress toward elimination from 2011 to 2025. The fourteen-year record shows how far the small kingdom has come — and what still stands in the way of zero cases.
plos-pone-0358455: Erythropoietin — the blood-boosting hormone — may also signal eye damage in diabetes. This LANDMark cohort study explored systemic erythropoietin in diabetic retinopathy, tracking longitudinal associations and biomarker potential. The hormone could become an early warning blood test for blinding disease.
plos-pone-0357755: Childhood leukemia evolves in stages — and mathematics can track its moves. This paper inferred stage-specific evolutionary dynamics in pediatric leukemia using Bayesian stochastic modeling. The models reveal how the cancer changes character as it progresses, informing when and how to strike it.
plos-pone-0350955: Alcohol use disorder impairs executive function — but how severely, and does it predict who recovers? This study compared patients with low psychiatric comorbidity against a non-clinical sample and tested executive function’s predictive value for treatment outcome. The cognitive profile it built can guide more targeted rehabilitation.
plos-pone-0356255: Women and mothers carry an invisible mental load — the endless background planning nobody sees. This paper examined the causes of distress, relevant personality traits, and psychopathology in mental load. The findings finally name and measure a burden that has gone unacknowledged for generations.
plos-pone-0355855: The antimicrobial peptide LL-37, better known for fighting germs, may also mark sleep quality. This clinical observational study linked plasma LL-37 levels to sleep quality in patients with obstructive sleep apnea. The peptide emerges as an unexpected biomarker candidate for disordered sleep.
plos-pone-0355955: Exosomes — tiny vesicles — secreted by brown versus white fat cells carry strikingly different messages. This paper showed they differentially regulate stemness, hormone secretion, apoptosis, and lipid metabolism in model cells. The vesicles reveal fat tissue as an active endocrine messenger, not just storage.
plos-pone-0357355: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper characterizing an AGAMOUS-like MADS box protein — a probable regulator of flowering and fruit ripening in banana. Readers should consult the corrected version for the accurate scientific record.
plos-pone-0355155: Contemporary Iraqi architecture is breaking new ground after decades of turmoil. This case study examined that architectural breakthrough — its forms, ideas, and ambitions. The buildings reflect a nation rebuilding its identity in concrete, glass, and cultural memory.
plos-pone-0347555: Asphalt mixtures crack in fiendishly complex ways at the mesoscale. This paper modeled mesostructural fracture with stochastic heterogeneity coupled to bilinear cohesive elements. The detailed modeling predicts how pavements will fail — helping engineers build roads that last longer.
plos-pone-0349155: Antiphospholipid syndrome — a clotting disorder — may yield to new drug targets. This systems pharmacology study revealed type I interferon and myeloid-like B cell reprogramming as candidate druggable axes. The computational findings nominate precise molecular targets for a disease with few good treatments.
plos-pone-0356955: This entry is an Expression of Concern, not a research finding. The journal has flagged the paper on constipation in Tg2576 Alzheimer’s mice, linked to dysregulation involving mAChR signaling pathways. The notice alerts readers that the paper’s reliability is under investigation.
plos-pone-0356055: Spatial neglect after stroke — ignoring half the world — resists conventional therapy. The EMPATH protocol outlines a randomized, double-blind trial of an engaging mobile prism adaptation treatment delivered at home and in rehab settings. The planned trial tests whether gamified prism therapy can reclaim the neglected half of space.
plos-pone-0354855: Acute rheumatic fever still damages young hearts — and future doctors must recognize it. This paper evaluated medical students’ awareness of the disease. The awareness gaps it found point to curriculum fixes that could save children from preventable heart damage.
plos-pone-0352555: Can AI design vocational curricula — and would anyone trust the results? This paper evaluated AI-generated curriculum designs in vocational education using a no-AI diagnostic assessment as evidence. The findings test whether machine-designed training actually teaches the hands-on skills trades demand.
plos-pone-0355655: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. The journal has retracted the paper claiming the herbal medicine KIOM-C induces autophagic and apoptotic cell death via JNK activation and reactive oxygen species in HT1080 human fibrosarcoma cells. The notice formally withdraws those findings.
plos-pone-0354755: Neotropical bats — from nectar-sippers to fruit-gorgers — process sugar in remarkably varied ways. This paper examined the physiological and ecological factors shaping sugar metabolism across species. The findings reveal how evolution tuned bat metabolism to match each species’ sugary niche.
plos-pone-0355055: For ventilated patients with tracheostomies, when to deflate the cuff matters. This observational study investigated cuff deflation timing in prolonged mechanical ventilation. The findings guide ICU teams toward weaning practices that restore speech and swallowing sooner — and more safely.
plos-pone-0353755: When home becomes a dangerous place — falls among community-dwelling elders — the costs cascade. This paper quantified the cost of falls among older people living at home. The economic analysis makes the fiscal case for prevention: grab bars and exercise programs are cheaper than hip fractures.
plos-pone-0354455: Power grid maintenance workers face scenario-specific occupational risks. This paper conducted scenario-based risk assessment for them. The structured assessment gives utilities the foresight to protect the workers who keep the lights on — often at great personal risk.
europmc-pmc2811155: Damaged mitochondria must be cleared before they poison the cell, and this 2010 paper reveals a key alarm system. The authors show the protein PINK1 sticks to impaired mitochondria and switches on Parkin, which tags them for removal. The PINK1-Parkin pathway became central to understanding Parkinson's disease, where this cleanup process fails.
europmc-pmc2814855: A cocktail of beneficial bacteria calmed an MS-like disease in this 2010 mouse study. The authors show a novel probiotic mixture eases experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by boosting regulatory T cells that make the calming signal IL-10. The result suggests gut microbes can tune the immune system. It opened a new angle on treating autoimmune disease through the microbiome.
europmc-pmc2815955: Nipah virus kept spilling from bats into people in Bangladesh, and this 2009 paper documents the pattern. The authors track recurrent zoonotic transmission from 2001 to 2007, mapping how and where infections jumped to humans. The surveillance revealed a steady, repeating threat. The study shaped efforts to interrupt transmission of this deadly virus.
europmc-pmc2846855: Drugs that cure mice routinely fail in people, raising an uncomfortable question. This 2010 paper asks whether animal models of disease can reliably inform human studies. The authors systematically assess the translational record. Their sobering analysis pushed for better-designed animal research instead of blind faith in mouse results.
europmc-pmc2939055: Parkinson's may show in the gut before the brain. This 2010 paper uses colonic biopsies to assess Parkinson's gut nerve damage and its link to symptoms. The authors find the disease's fingerprints in the bowel. Their work supports gut-first diagnosis.
europmc-pmc3000155: A newly found virus sickened Hong Kong children. This 2003 paper links a fresh virus, metapneumovirus, to child breathing illness in Hong Kong. The authors document the outbreak cases. Their work established the virus's role. Labs added it to routine winter panels.
europmc-pmc3004955: Brain scans got blazing fast. This 2010 paper brings a scan trick that images the whole brain in under a second. The authors' speedup transformed brain imaging. Their method spread through labs. Babies and fidgety patients benefit most. Whole-brain movies now run in real time.
europmc-pmc3018455: Drug rashes can peel skin clean off. This 2010 review covers toxic epidermal necrolysis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome. The authors survey these skin emergencies. Their overview guides urgent burn-like care. Common painkillers can trigger the reaction. Gene tests now flag at-risk patients.
europmc-pmc3024255: Gene network modules need a quality check. This 2011 paper asks if network modules hold up across datasets. The authors' stats test each module's staying power. Their tool spread through labs. Shaky modules get flagged before publication. The test runs in the popular WGCNA package.
europmc-pmc3101655: Grip strength got population norms. This 2011 study tables normal grip strength by age and sex. The authors' charts guide clinicians. Their work aids frailty screening. Weak grips flag frailty early. A squeeze test takes ten seconds. Clinics now track grips yearly.
europmc-pmc3102055: Desk jobs fattened America. This 2011 paper tracks fifty years of shrinking workplace activity and rising obesity. The authors' data explains the epidemic. Their work shaped workplace health. Workers now burn 100 fewer calories daily. Standing desks grew from this finding.
europmc-pmc6547655: Worn-out senescent cells pile up with age and should be cleared by the immune system - yet they persist. Researchers found their trick: the cells display HLA-E, a molecular 'do not eat me' flag that switches off attacking NK and CD8 T cells. The discovery explains a piece of aging and points to drugs that could strip the disguise.
europmc-pmc6582955: Single-cell RNA sequencing reads gene activity one cell at a time - powerful, but the analysis maze overwhelms newcomers. This tutorial lays out current best practices step by step: quality checks, normalization, clustering, and how to avoid classic traps. New analysts get a trusted path from raw cell data to reliable biology.
europmc-pmc6591855: Drug-resistant tuberculosis is a global menace, and spotting resistance fast saves lives. This paper pairs pocket-size nanopore sequencers with smart software that reads TB genomes and flags drug-resistance mutations on the spot. The combo brings rapid, field-ready resistance testing to clinics that need it most.
europmc-pmc6592155: Great health programs fail when nobody uses them right - implementation is half the battle. Implementation Mapping adapts a classic planning method to design rollout strategies step by step: who needs to do what, and what will help them. The framework turns 'just do it' into a science of getting innovations adopted.
europmc-pmc6691855: Fiber feeds gut bacteria - and their exhaust may tune blood sugar. In a small human trial, delivering propionate (a bacterial product) to the colon via inulin improved insulin sensitivity in overweight adults. The study traces the chain: fiber to microbes to metabolites to better glucose control.
europmc-pmc6712955: Depression may smolder with low-grade inflammation - measurable in a simple blood test for CRP. Pooling studies in a systematic review and meta-analysis, researchers pinned down how common raised CRP is among depressed patients. The numbers strengthen the case for anti-inflammatory strategies in psychiatry.
europmc-pmc6716655: For rural patients, a video call can replace a grueling road trip to the clinic. This systematic review asked whether patients and caregivers are actually satisfied with telehealth videoconferencing. The answer: largely yes - the screen delivers care that feels personal enough.
europmc-pmc6731555: Neoantigens are the immune system's most wanted - protein fragments found on tumors but nowhere else. This review traces their journey from basic discovery to clinical use: how they are found, how vaccines target them, and where trials stand. The truly foreign flags promise truly personal therapy.
europmc-pmc6748955: Gut microbes differ between the merely obese and the metabolically ill - but the markers disagree across studies. This research article hunts consistent microbial signatures for classifying obesity-related metabolic trouble. Reliable markers would sharpen both diagnosis and treatment.
europmc-pmc6761255: Quality of life means different things to different fields - a muddle for medicine. This systematic review surveyed QOL research across medicine and health sciences: how the concept is defined, measured, and used. The map brings order to a sprawling, slippery literature.
europmc-pmc6770155: Berries and tea feed more than you - they feed your gut microbes. This review explores dietary polyphenols' two-way traffic with the microbiome: how microbes unlock the compounds' benefits and how to deliver them more efficiently. The gut, it turns out, is a co-chef in nutrition.
europmc-pmc6778655: Pilot studies are science's dress rehearsals - and sloppy reporting wastes them. These guidelines set standards for reporting non-randomized pilot and feasibility studies. The checklist helps researchers write reports that actually guide the main event.
gao-gaoreports-b-309955: A 2007 GAO ruling on a contract fight from Nautical Engineering, Inc. The marine firm said the agency's pick broke the rules of fair bidding; the ruling puts each claim to the test. Published rulings like this guide the next round — they tell agencies and bidders alike where the legal lines are drawn.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-655: The fire agencies were fighting blind in 2007 — GAO's report says no clear goals or strategy guided the costly war on wildfire. The findings describe big spending without a compass. The report demands what every campaign needs: know what winning looks like before you pay for it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-555: Poor seniors were missing their drug discount in 2007 — GAO's report says Social Security needed to push harder on outreach for the low-income drug subsidy. The findings measure the enrollment gap. The report's plea: the cheapest benefit is the one people actually claim.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-455: Homeland Security's many networks were talking past each other in 2007 — GAO's report says the federal systems needed to be better joined up. The findings demand the wiring be linked. The report's point: a homeland split in its data cannot stand secure.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-355: Employers were trimming health and pension perks in 2007 — GAO's report tracks the cost-cutting and what it meant for workers. The findings map the squeeze in detail. The report's warning: the shrinking benefit was the quiet pay cut of the decade.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-255: The bank insurer's people programs looked sound in 2007, and GAO's report says the human capital and risk efforts appeared solid, though evaluation lagged. The findings credit the design. The report's nudge: good programs still need proof they work. The proof had to follow the promise.
openalex-w7206185255: Robotic exoskeletons, wearable frames that help people move, are advancing fast in Brazil. This article reviews a decade of development, with special attention to rehabilitation uses and to biosensors like EMG electrodes that read muscle signals to guide the device. The authors explain how sensor integration is making these machines more responsive to the wearer's body. A survey of a technology that is moving from labs toward clinics and workplaces.
openalex-w7204999855: Kids who move more tend to be healthier in body and mind, yet inactivity keeps rising. This paper reports on a project that set out to teach young people why exercise matters, connecting physical activity to chronic disease, obesity, and mental well-being. The authors describe the awareness effort and its reception. Simple in premise and earnest in execution, it makes the case for movement as preventive medicine.
openalex-w7205008855: University life tests more than intellect; it tests how students handle people, pressure, and independence. This study examines the link between social skills and mental health in college students, asking whether students with stronger interpersonal repertoires cope better. The authors frame social skills as a resource for navigating academic and personal demands. Relevant to counselors, educators, and anyone who remembers freshman year.
openalex-w7205015755: Tired doctors make more mistakes. This study looks at how lack of sleep harms the thinking, focus, and split-second choices of health workers on long shifts. The authors review the effects on medical errors and on the workers' own mental and physical health. A sobering reminder that the people who care for patients around the clock pay a price in their own bodies and minds.
openalex-w7204642155: Heart surgery stopped and restarted at Brasilia's main public hospital, right as COVID hit. This article profiles 188 patients who had heart operations there from late 2019 through 2022, covering the service's revival and the pandemic years. The authors map who was treated and how they fared. A rare institutional portrait of cardiac care under extraordinary strain.
openalex-w7171682655: Muscles fade with age, and doctors need better ways to spot it. This paper proposes a four-gene panel for detecting aged, senescent cell states in muscle tissue. The authors targeted sarcopenia diagnostics. A geroscience study of reading aging in genes.
pmc-13439655: A 2026 chemistry paper investigating the crystallization of a hydroxycarbonate precursor for a nickel-magnesium catalyst using in situ and ex situ methods. Watching crystals form in real time reveals how catalyst structure emerges. The study informs better catalyst manufacturing.
pmc-13389355: This 2026 physics primer explains photon-counting detectors in CT — how they work, how signals form, and how they perform. Photon-counting is the next leap in CT imaging, promising sharper images at lower dose. The primer makes the physics accessible to medical physicists and radiologists.
pmc-13375155: This 2026 in vitro study compared the initial cytotoxicity of resin-based materials for interim dental prostheses made by additive (3D printing) versus subtractive (milling) manufacturing. How a crown is made may affect its biocompatibility. The head-to-head test gives dentists data.
pmc-13439955: This 2026 C. elegans paper revealed bidirectional cross-talk between the heat shock response and the endoplasmic reticulum stress response (UPRER) under heat stress. The two stress systems talk back and forth, not just in parallel. The finding rewrites the stress-response wiring diagram.
pmc-13470255: This 2026 case report used multimodality imaging to diagnose a pericardial lipoma — a fatty tumor around the heart — encasing the right coronary artery. The benign tumor's dangerous location made imaging critical. The case shows how combined modalities solve tricky cardiac diagnoses.
pmc-13452155: A 2026 case report on biochemical discordance of a urinary fluoroquinolone-resistant E. coli ST1193 identified as a Shigella species. The misidentification had clinical consequences. The case warns microbiologists.
pmc-13423955: In this 2026 study, the Global Alignment and Proportion (GAP) score showed limited predictive performance for mechanical complications in older Asian patients with adult spinal deformity. The Western-derived score didn't transfer. The finding calls for population-specific tools.
pmc-13448255: A 2026 conference abstract (TPRG-01) describing TRIO-MBM — a multicenter phase II trial of relatlimab, nivolumab, and ipilimumab in melanoma brain metastasis patients. The triple immunotherapy was tested. The abstract outlines the trial.
pmc-13448455: A 2026 conference abstract (PACM-06) on laser interstitial thermal therapy in a porcine spine tumor model — a promising alternative to separation surgery for metastatic epidural disease. The pig model tested the laser approach. The abstract reports the promise.
pmc-13529155: A 2026 nursing study of challenges and successes in caring for Syrian refugees. The refugee nurses' perspective is rare. The study documents both struggles and wins.
pmc-13494555: In this 2026 evolution paper, the evolutionary fitness of specific synonymous codon changes was estimated. The "silent" mutations weren't neutral. The fitness estimates reframe codon usage.
pmc-13459155: This 2026 mouse study found chronic Toxoplasma gondii infection attenuated tau hyperphosphorylation in an Alzheimer's model. The parasite paradoxically protected against tau. The attenuation is the surprising result.
pmc-13458955: A 2026 2-year prospective analysis from the UK Medical Cannabis Registry on cannabis-based medicinal products for endometriosis. The cannabis products' real-world effects were tracked. The analysis is the evidence.
pmc-13580755: A 2026 pharmaceutics paper on sex-related differences in physiologically-based biopharmaceutics modeling. The drug models differed by sex. The differences matter for dosing.
pmc-13416755: A 2026 data-driven paper on dynamic co-evolution of obesity-metabolic-inflammatory factors for cardiovascular risk stratification in middle-aged and older adults (the title is truncated). The risk trajectories were modeled. The stratification is the clinical tool.
pmc-13365355: A 2026 randomized controlled trial of calcium HMB-enriched nutritional supplementation during dietary weight loss in adults with obesity (the title is truncated). The supplement's body composition effects were tested. The trial is the evidence.
pmc-13353355: In this 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis, the association between fat-free mass and mortality was synthesized. The muscle-mortality link was quantified. The association is the prognostic signal.
pmc-13291755: A 2026 statistical analysis plan for the Danish Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Trial. The trial's analysis was pre-specified. The plan is the methodological transparency.
pmc-13479555: In this 2026 network analysis, symptom-level pathways between fear of missing out and mobile phone addiction were unveiled among Chinese college students. The FOMO-addiction links were mapped. The pathways are the finding.
pmc-13429255: A 2026 study of factors predicting loneliness in older adults attending Delaware senior center programs. The loneliness drivers were identified. The factors guide intervention.
pmc-13427755: This 2026 randomized dose escalation study tested inhaled LTI-03 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The inhaled therapy's dosing was explored. The study is the early evidence.
pmc-13426455: In this 2026 neuroscience paper, elevating cerebellar theta oscillations boosted noninvasively induced motor plasticity. The brain stimulation's effect was amplified. The boosting is the mechanism.
pmc-13492855: A 2026 quasi-experimental study improving iron deficiency anemia knowledge through a nurse-led educational program among adolescent girls. The nurses taught effectively. The improving is the outcome.
pmc-13441155: This 2026 paper reported patient-centered, coordinated therapy with RNA interference-based givosiran for acute hepatic porphyria — real-life experience for an ultra-rare disease (the title is truncated). The gene silencer's real-world use was documented. The experience is the evidence.
pmc-13522455: A 2026 green chemistry paper: recoverable macroporous polyanion bead catalysts for scalable continuous chemical depolymerization of PET. The plastic-eating beads were reusable. The catalysts serve recycling.
pmc-13462255: This 2026 paper characterized long non-coding RNAs during compatible and incompatible pollination in Arabidopsis thaliana. The plant's pollination lncRNAs were profiled. The characterizing is the reproductive biology.
pmc-13418855: A 2026 study of frailty's association with transfusions, hospitalizations, and survival in myelodysplastic syndrome patients initiating hypomethylating agents. The frailty's prognostic weight was quantified. The association guides hematology.
pmc-13489555: In this 2026 Drosophila paper, the ecdysone receptor autonomously controlled germ cell differentiation in the ovary. The hormone receptor's germline role was defined. The controlling is the developmental mechanism.
arxiv-2606-15955: One idea for cooling the planet is to spray tiny bits high in the sky so they bounce sunlight back to space. This paper designs special ultra-small solid bits meant to make that idea safer and easier to control. The focus is on the bits themselves — what they are made of and how they act.
arxiv-2606-16055: Reading out a quantum bit in a superconducting circuit can accidentally kick it into an unwanted state — "readout-induced leakage." This experimental physics paper studies that leakage in circuits with nonlinear couplings, which make the effect trickier. The findings help engineers design quantum computers where measuring a qubit doesn't corrupt it.
arxiv-2606-16255: Most AI eyes either read pics or dream them — few do both well. UniDDT weds both crafts in one frame: a split-brain dream engine whose halves still pull as one. The paper hands pic-AI builders a true two-way maker.
arxiv-2606-16455: Researchers often need to find hidden subgroups in data mixing continuous measurements and yes/no answers. hyreg2 is an R package that estimates latent classes on such mixed data — clustering people or samples into unobserved groups. The paper presents the software for statisticians and social scientists doing mixture modeling.
arxiv-2606-16555: Cloud platforms orchestrate services with learned policies, but those policies need the right incentives — and evidence that they work. This paper studies incentives and evidence in learned service orchestration: how to reward orchestrators and verify their decisions. It targets researchers in cloud computing and AI-driven systems management.
arxiv-2606-16655: In federated learning, devices train together without sharing raw data — but one-shot versions (a single round) struggle when devices' data differ wildly. This paper aligns their distributions using optimal transport, the mathematics of moving mass efficiently. It targets researchers making single-round federated learning actually work.
arxiv-2606-16855: Beaming internet through the air with lasers (free-space optics) suffers when heat shimmer scrambles the beam. This paper cuts turbulence-induced outages on a real deployed terrestrial link. It is for optical communications engineers. Steady beams, fewer blackouts. Field fixes beat lab fixes.
